claim: Volkswagen Arena holds 30,000 (8,000 standing), Wolfsburg typically sells out a third to half of home matches, and matchday ticket prices range from €15 standing to €44 seated in Category 3, climbing to €35–€70 for higher-demand fixtures.
quote: Capacity: 30,000 (8,000 standing) ... Wolfsburg tend to sell out about a third to half of their home matches

claim: The AOK Stadion has been the home of the VfL Wolfsburg women's team since 2015 and holds up to 5,200 spectators.
quote: AOK Stadion ... has been the home stadium for the VfL Ladies since 2015 and houses up to 5,200 Wolves fans

claim: VfL Wolfsburg Frauen day tickets at the AOK Stadion range from €9 standing to €17 seated for Category 2 matches and €6–€15 for Category 3 — far cheaper than the men's Bundesliga tickets.
quote: Seated areas (W1-W5): €17.00 regular / €12.00 reduced ... Standing areas (N1, N2, S1): €10.00 regular / €7.00 reduced

claim: VfL Wolfsburg's women's team has won 7 Bundesliga titles, 11 DFB-Pokal trophies and back-to-back UEFA Women's Champions League titles in 2013 and 2014, ranking them among Europe's elite.
quote: VfL Wolfsburg has won 7 Bundesliga championships and 11 DFB-Pokal titles ... won the UEFA Women's Champions League in 2013 and 2014

claim: Public guided stadium tours of the Volkswagen Arena run Monday–Saturday at 2pm from the VfL fan store at the arena, last about 90 minutes and take visitors through the press room, dugouts and VIP areas; cancelled on Sundays, holidays and the day before men's home matches.
quote: The stadium tours take place Monday to Saturday at 2.00 pm, with the tour starting at the VfL fan store ... approximately 90 minutes

claim: Stadium tours cost €7 for adults (over 16) and €5 for children/concessions, with under-fives free; no prior registration is required at the fan-shop meeting point.
quote: €7.00 for adults (over 16s) and €5.00 for children and concessions, with kids under five receiving free entry

claim: The Volkswagen Arena sits about a kilometre from Wolfsburg Hauptbahnhof and roughly 3 km from the main city centre, a 15–20-minute walk via the rail tracks and canal.
quote: approximately 15 minutes to walk from Wolfsburg Hauptbahnhof train station to the Volkswagen Arena ... just under 3km from the main city centre

claim: Planetarium Wolfsburg admission is €9.50 for adults and €7 for children/students/disabled visitors, with a 25% family discount; premium music shows run €12–€17.
quote: Adults: €9.50 ... Children, students, disabled visitors, and unemployment benefit recipients: €7.00 ... Musikshows ... €12.00 to €17.00

claim: The Planetarium offers live-narrated star shows plus themed music programmes such as Space Tour (pop/rock journey to the stars) and Sternzeit (classical compositions by Beethoven, Vivaldi, Tchaikovsky), with regular daily showings.
quote: live-moderated star shows and lecture programs on astronomical and geological topics ... Space Tour ... STERNZEIT ... Stars of Classic

claim: Grizzlys Wolfsburg DEL ice-hockey single-game tickets for the 2025/26 season start at €22.00 and can be bought online, at the Eis Arena fan shop or at presale outlets.
quote: Tickets start from €22.00 for games during the 2025/2026 season

claim: Eis Arena Wolfsburg holds up to 4,500 (about 3,000 seats, 1,500 standing) for Grizzlys home games, with the season's end tied to how far the team progresses in the DEL playoffs.
quote: about 3,000 seats in the arena, 300 of which are in the VIP area ... standing room for approximately 1,500 people ... end of the ice skating season ... depends on how far the Grizzlies get in the playoffs

claim: BadeLand Wolfsburg, sitting next to the Eis Arena in the 130-hectare Allerpark, is northern Germany's largest family pool at 22,000 m² with a Black Hole flume, wave pool, lazy river and twelve saunas — a strong wet-weather family option.
quote: northern Germany's largest leisure and family pool ... 22,000 square meters ... 'Black Hole' flume ... lazy river and a large wave pool ... Twelve saunas

claim: The free-admission Tiergehege Wolfsburg, in a former quarry by Klinikum Wolfsburg, keeps small farm and exotic birds (ducks, peacocks, budgerigars, cockatiels, pheasants), rabbits and guinea pigs — a low-key kids' stop open 8:30–15:30.
quote: ducks, geese, budgerigars and cockatiels, pheasants, chickens, peacocks as well as rabbits and guinea pigs. Admission to the Tiergehege Wolfsburg is free!

claim: VfL Wolfsburg opened the 2025/26 Bundesliga campaign on 23 August 2025 away at Heidenheim and closed on 16 May 2026 at St. Pauli; the men have struggled with relegation pressure after conceding 53 goals.
quote: Wolfsburg kick off their Bundesliga campaign 2025/26 on Saturday 23 August with an away match against Heidenheim ... final matchday takes place on 16 May 2026

claim: The Allerpark complex bundles free family kit — beach-volleyball court, skate sculpture, the climb-and-balance Bodenlos treetop playground, outdoor fitness gear — alongside paid options like B'MOOVD bowling, BadeLand and the Eis Arena.
quote: free activities such as a beach volleyball court, a skate sculpture and play and climbing facilities for children to outdoor fitness equipment, the EisArena, BadeLand and B'MOOVD Sportsbar & Bowling
